I have been really impressed with AnythingLLM as a no-fuss way to use LLMs locally and via APIs. For those of us who want to tinker, there's a solid range of choice for embedders and vector stores. The single install desktop packaging is very slick.
I had a much smoother experience with the desktop version of AnythingLLM. There's more in openwebui, but the things that are in AnythingLLM are more polished (IMO).

This is really nice. My first reaction was 'oh great, another Ollama/WebGenUI wrapper on Llama.cpp' but it's actually much more - supporting not only the LLM but also embedding models, vector databases, and TTS/STT.
As someone who doesn't know what an Embed or Vector is, this has been the only offline AI tool I've been able to install and start using on my standard office PC.
This definitely makes it super easy for less technical folks to access it (got it up and running in less than 5 minutes). Initial reaction is positive with just Ollama.

Downloaded and checked it out on regulatory PDFs with GPT-4o: citations seem to be a bit dicey - largely correct answers but citations window shows content that's a bit garbled. Also requested a chat history search feature.
There was an error while installing on Linux, solved with: sudo chown root:root .../chrome-sandbox && sudo chmod 4755 .../chrome-sandbox. Other than that it worked really well.
$ docker pull mintplexlabs/anythingllm ... Error response from daemon: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
I just wish there was an option to properly include custom CSS. The default interface looks a little bit.. dated.
I've been attempting to deploy a customized AnythingLLM instance within an enterprise env. TimC (and presumably dev crew) are top notch and very responsive. Waiting for EntraID integration.
How do you ensure 'privacy by default' if you are also providing cloud models? [Dev clarified: defaults are private/local, external LLM/embedder/vector-db usage is opt-in per component.]
